messages:
alex_w: heads-up — since ~10:12 UTC our Trivy scanner workers started failing on KMS decrypt ops, causing the scanner-connector to backoff and GHAS/Snyk webhooks to pile up. logs: `error=rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = requestor does not have permission to decrypt`

devops-bot: deploy 2025-06-11T10:05 by @maria_s applied: iam-policy-update svc-account:scanner-sa removed role:roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter (auto-change) :rotating_light:

maria_s: yep that change landed as part of iam tidy PR #3421 — intended to tighten perms on a dev-only SA. I missed that scanner-sa was in the exception list. my bad.

jon: can we confirm it's the exact denied permission? alex_w can you paste the minimal error stack from scanner?

alex_w: snippet: 
```
2025-06-11T10:12:08Z scanner-connector[replica-3]: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = requestor does not have permission to decrypt on projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/scanner/cryptoKeys/scan-key/cryptoKeyVersions/1
2025-06-11T10:12:08Z scanner-connector[replica-3]: failed to decrypt token for registry auth, marking task as retryable
```

irene: can you check Cloud Audit Logs for the IAM change? we need who/when for postmortem and for compliance audit.

maria_s: looking. change created by me at 2025-06-11T10:05 via terraform apply. I have the PR and plan. I didn't realize scanner-sa used that key; it's referenced by `scanner-connector` config.

snyk-bot: WARNING incoming webhook backlog (GHAS->Snyk) 429 x-retries, last-response: `{"status":429,"retry-after":6}`. Delivery queue length=218.

security-oncall: mitigation options: 1) rollback the IAM change (fast) 2) grant kms.decrypt back to scanner-sa (medium) 3) rotate to a new key and update config (slow). prefer rollback for now to restore scanning and then plan permanent fix.

jon: rollback sounds right. we also need to make a short-term suppression to avoid flooding alerts for duplicate vuln findings while queue drains. put a suppression rule for `KMS_DECRYPT_FAILURE` on the pipeline alerts.

devops: rolling back now — terraform apply targeting iam-policy for scanner-sa. ETA ~5m. I'll also throttle webhook delivery on the connector to avoid hammering Snyk endpoints.

alex_w: noted. adding temporary alert suppression locally: `alertmanager silence add --match='alertname="ScannerKMSDecrypt"' --duration=2h --created-by='eng-security'`

maria_s: created jira SEC-8421 to track root cause + permissions inventory. assigning to me for remediation and to add a test in terraform CI to detect removal of required roles for known service accounts. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-8421

devops-bot: terraform apply complete — scanner-sa IAM policy reverted.

alex_w: scanner connector logs now show success: `decrypted token, starting scan` and upstream webhook backlog draining. first successful scan at 10:21:04Z.

irene: for the postmortem we'll need timeline, who authorized account changes, and why scanner-sa wasn't listed in the exceptions doc. also add KMS audit entries to the ticket.

jon: follow-ups we should add to SEC-8421: 1) CI check that validates service account permissions vs a saved manifest 2) add unit test in scanner to surface KMS permission errors earlier (fail fast) 3) make scanner use a token cache to reduce KMS calls 4) add a runbook entry for IAM changes that alerts security when a policy touches scanner-sa or keys named `scanner*`

security-oncall: created a postmortem stub in the ticket. recommend we also add `kms.decrypt` denial as a classified non-actionable noise for webhook dedupe while we fix infra, so downstream Snyk/GHAS don't create duplicate findings.

devops: will also add an alert when `iam.policy_changed` touches `scanner-sa` so changes cannot be applied without a review tag.

maria_s: sorry again about the slip. I'll get the terraform module updated with explicit `required_roles` and add a pre-apply hook to warn.

alex_w: thanks all — monitoring until backlog cleared. if anything flaps I'll post here. :thumbsup:
